root_cause_label: make clean deleted required output files; executables rebuilt but never re-run to regenerate serial.out and pgen_*.out
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent built working serial and pgen binaries and produced correct output files, but `make clean` at step 151 deleted all output files and the trajectory ended at step 152 (make rebuilt binaries only) without ever re-running `./serial test` or `./pgen test` to regenerate the required output artifacts.
t_err_evidence: Step 151: `make clean` executed successfully with output `rm -f serial pgen /app/serial.out /app/pgen_*.out /app/*_sorted.out /app/parallel_combined.out`, explicitly deleting all required output files. The Makefile clean target (authored at step 150) included these output files, but the agent ran make clean without planning to re-run the executables afterward.
t_commit_evidence: Step 152: `make` successfully rebuilt the serial and pgen binaries (`gcc -O2 -pthread -o serial serial.c; gcc -O2 -pthread -o pgen pgen.c`) but the trajectory ends here with no subsequent `./serial test` or `./pgen test` commands. The output files serial.out and pgen_*.out no longer exist at evaluation time.
trigger_explanation: The Makefile clean target (visible at step 142 and step 150) explicitly listed `rm -f serial pgen /app/serial.out /app/pgen_*.out /app/*_sorted.out /app/parallel_combined.out`. The agent wrote this rule itself and saw its output at step 151, yet proceeded without recognizing that the required output files had been destroyed and needed to be regenerated by re-running the executables against the test input.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 143-147 show repeated `Makefile:9: *** missing separator. Stop.` errors when running make clean and make, indicating the Makefile was broken. These errors foreshadowed that the cleanup/rebuild loop (steps 143-152) would become the agent's focus, displacing attention from regenerating output files after any successful clean.
